creator: opichillc
title: Set up a global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (30-50 lines of personal conventions) that layers with each project's CLAUDE.md

tools.name: Claude Code global CLAUDE.md
tools.detail: file in the home directory (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) read at the start of every session

claims: A global CLAUDE.md in your home directory is read automatically at the start of every session in every project
Project-level CLAUDE.md handles codebase specifics; the global one handles you; Claude reads both and they layer
Keep the global file short: 30-50 lines
Next video promises one command that teaches Claude your whole project structure in seconds
how_to_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in the home directory's .claude folder
Put in cross-project preferences: coding style, git conventions (e.g. conventional commits), preferred frameworks (e.g. TypeScript over JavaScript), 'run tests before committing'
Keep project-specific context in each repo's CLAUDE.md
Keep the global file to the things you'd tell a new teammate on day one
on_screen_only: Persistent banner: 'Don't skip this Claude Code feature!'
cta: DM or book a call via link in bio

relevance.why: Correct but basic; a veteran Claude Code user almost certainly already has a global CLAUDE.md

implement_score.why: Five-minute task if not already done; worth a quick audit that the global file is still under ~50 lines given the 'thin CLAUDE.md' advice

verify: Exact path is ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (creator says 'home directory' and points at the screen without naming it)

gap.what: Only adds the global-vs-project CLAUDE.md layering and a 30-50 line budget; minor next to the liked 'keep CLAUDE.md thin' content
